KP 2. Expressing a Definite Integral as the Limit of a Left Riemann Sum
3.?

What is ∫15x−1dx expressed as the limit of a left Riemann sum?

M
Fri, Sep 4th @ 1:43 PM|Elapsed: 5:17Correct

The definite integral can be defined in terms of the limit of a left Riemann sum as ∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑i=0n−1f(xi)⋅Δx,

where Δx=b−an and xi=a+iΔx.

In the definite integral ∫15x−1dx, the function is f(x)=x−1, the lower bound is a=1, and the upper bound is b=5. So, we have Δx=5−1n=4n,

and therefore ∫15x−1dx=limn→∞∑i=0n−1f(xi)⋅Δx=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[f(1+i⋅4n)⋅4n]=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[f(1+4in)⋅4n]=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[1+4in−1⋅4n]=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[4in⋅4n]=limn→∞∑i=0n−1[in⋅8n].

KP 3. Expressing the Limit of a Left Riemann Sum as a Definite Integral
7.?

Find the function f(x) and the value of b, given that ∫−π/4bf(x)dx=limn→∞∑l=0n−1[sec2⁡(−π4+πl2n)⋅π2n].

H
Fri, Sep 4th @ 2:03 PM|Elapsed: 10:18Correct

A definite integral can be defined as the limit of a left Riemann sum as follows: ∫abf(x)dx=limn→∞∑l=0n−1f(xl)⋅Δx where Δx=b−an and xl=a+lΔx.

Notice that we're given that the lower limit a=−π4.

Comparing the given summation with the general expression above, we see that Δx=π2n. Therefore, π2n=(b−(−π4))n⟹b=π4.

Consequently, xl=−π4+πl2n and f(xl)=sec2⁡xl.

Hence, ∫−π/4π/4sec2⁡xdx=limn→∞∑l=0n−1[sec2⁡(−π4+πl2n)⋅π2n].

Therefore, the correct answer is f(x)=sec2⁡x and b=π4.
